description: This is my worldgen mod for Minecraft. There are many like it, but this one is mine.

mods.name: Big Globe
mods.description: Round earth is a hoax invented by Big Globe to sell more globes!

releases.notes:
# For normal users
* Fully re-implemented the "islands" world preset.
	* Each island has a different type associated with it.
	* Each island type can be thought of as like a different biome, with a different set of terrain gen parameters.
* Performance improvements.
* Sand, gravel, and other falling blocks now work differently in Big Globe worlds.
	* This is because there's sometimes a lot of it underground in cave ceilings, and having it all fall at once is laggy.
* Fixed lava replacing blocks that it shouldn't near lava level in the nether.
* Dry lakes now only spawn in deserts.
	* Likewise, non-dry lakes now only spawn outside of deserts.
* Minor visual tweak: aura-infused clouds now have AO, like regular clouds do.
* Added UNSUPPORTED mixin `ChunkPyramid_ConfigurableFeatureRadius` to expand the max size of configured features.
	* This mixin may be unstable, and may break things in subtle and hard-to-debug ways.
	* This mixin will make worldgen noticeably slower when exploring.
	* This mixin will never be enabled by default.
	* Nevertheless, it can be used to make my trees spawn correctly in pre-generated worlds, without needing to get near them first, which may be desirable when combined with LODs.
	* A value of 4 is required for my largest trees. The max value is 8, and the mixin will be completely disabled when set to a negative value or 0.
	* If you use this mixin, you are not allowed to report bugs with anything to anyone.
# For data pack developers
* The concept of column restrictions has been replaced with scripts.
	* This affects flowers, trees with fungal shelves, and rock layers.
	* Reason: the existing column restriction system was too limited (it didn't even have a dedicated type for world traits), too verbose, slower than it needed to be, and required a lot of maintenance. Scripts are just better in every possible way.
* Removed legacy handling of `minecraft:grass` and `minecraft:chain` blocks.
	* These were renamed in vanilla a long time ago to `minecraft:short_grass` and `minecraft:iron_chain` respectively.
	* Big Globe would previously accept the old names too, for scripts that needed to work in multiple MC versions.
	* However, Big Globe no longer supports MC versions where these legacy names were in-use, so support for the legacy names is now removed.

releases.notes:
# For normal users
* Fixed Iris compatibility on NeoForge (via Sinytra Connector or Launchpad).
* Fixed wildflowers not spawning correctly.
* Tweaked mob spawns in the "inferno" biome:
	* Blazes are now less likely.
	* Magma cubes are now more likely.
* Changed biome sky colors again.
* Very small visual tweak: AO on molten rock is now inversely proportional to its heat level.
# For data pack developers
* Some biome tags were moved around or renamed to better describe their purpose.
	* "overworld_except_volcano" -> "all_overworld"
	* "overworld" -> "all_islands"
	* "land_except_volcano" -> "land_overworld"
	* "land" -> "land_islands"
	* Probably a couple others that I forgot too.
# For no one in particular
* The "Islands" world preset is now roughly half-implemented.
	* It still won't show up in the world creation screen, but data packs can change this. If you know how to make such a data pack, feel free to test the Islands world preset in its current (unfinished) form!
	* Each island has its own biome and shape now.
	* Many decorations (including ores) are still missing.

releases.notes:
* Fixed bug causing everyone to get mostly the same world regardless of the world seed.
	* This bug primarily affects noise generation, which contributes the most to terrain shape.
		* Other smaller things like erosion patterns, structure placement positions, and so on are not affected, as they use the correct world seed.
	* This bug went un-noticed for quite some time due to the fact that the player spawn radius is so large by default, so everyone spawned in a different area of the same world.
	* A config option has been provided to keep this behavior un-changed to avoid breaking old worlds.
		* It defaults to the old (broken) behavior if you updated from a version containing this bug, and defaults to the new (fixed) behavior if you are running a fresh install.
* Now compatible with Launchpad by default. Launchpad is basically "Sinytra Connector lite", and may be more stable than Sinytra Connector is.
	* I haven't personally tested this, but at least one user claims it works. Let me know if you have any issues with it.

releases.notes:
# For regular users
* No changes.
# For data pack developers
* `/bigglobe:dumpRegistries` command now organizes files by the same folder structure as Minecraft.
	* This allows them to be loaded by the GlobeScript Intellij plugin.
# For no one in particular
* Some mixins that conflict with NeoForge (via Sinytra Connector) have now been fixed or auto-disabled.
	* This does NOT mean that Big Globe works correctly when running with Sinytra Connector yet, but it is a step in the right direction.

releases.notes:
* Fixed LODs on AMD (again).
* Fixed blindness and darkness debuffs not working when LODs are enabled.
* Fixed portal temple sometimes not spawning correctly.
* Fixed `/bigglobe:respawn` command spamming stack traces when typing the mode.
* Fixed environment attributes in pale garden biome. Among other things, this means the fog color is correct now.
* Slightly improved hyperspace collapse visuals.
